svg.title: The checkpoint write gate, amended so a deleted file is rewritten
svg.desc: The per-tick hook forms a place from the stream path, the byte offset, the stream's device and inode, and the reported map. If that place differs from the place this arming last wrote, the checkpoint is written. If the place is equal, the gate asks a second question that the original gate never asked: does the checkpoint file still exist? When the file is present nothing is written, so an idle arming leaves the filesystem quiet. When the file is gone, the checkpoint is written again on this poll, so a file deleted while the pane sat idle is restored rather than staying absent until the stream next moves.
svg.text: poll tick: form the place from four parts
path · offset · device and inode · reported map
equal to the place last written?
compared against this arming's own memory
does the checkpoint file still exist?
the question the original gate never asked
no — deleted under an idle pane
idle arming leaves the filesystem quiet
sibling temp file, flush and fsync, rename over the target, directory fsync —
then remember the place, so the next poll sees the file present again
Both routes reach the write: a moved place, or a place that did not move but whose file is gone.
A checkpoint removed while the pane sat idle comes back on the very next poll, so a reload in that
window still finds the pane's memory instead of losing it.
